accepted.question_text: Consider gradient descent on a convex function f: R^d -> R that is L-smooth, meaning that its gradient exists and is L-Lipschitz. Starting from an initial point x0 in R^d, the iterates are defined by x_{t+1} = x_t - eta_t nabla f(x_t), and f* = inf f with x* denoting a minimizer. What is the best anytime convergence rate for the individual-iterate error f(x_T) - f* that can be guaranteed uniformly over all such objectives by choosing a stepsize sequence (eta_t)_{t=0}^infinity? In particular, does there exist a stepsize sequence and an exponent alpha > 1 such that, for every horizon T in N and every L-smooth convex function f, the error f(x_T) - f* is bounded up to a universal constant factor by L ||x0 - x*||^2 / T^alpha, with the guarantee available in an anytime, monotonically decreasing form across all T?
accepted.context_brief: Anytime acceleration for gradient descent on smooth convex objectives

evidence.quote: Given a convex function f : R^d -> R which is L-smooth (i.e. nabla f exists and is L-Lipschitz), and an initial point x0 in R^d, the GD iterates with stepsizes (eta_t)^infinity_{t=0} are defined as x_{t+1} = x_t - eta_t nabla f(x_t).

Open Problem 1 What is the best anytime convergence rate achievable by GD with some stepsize sequence (eta_t)^infinity_{t=0}, uniformly over L-smooth convex functions? In particular, is there any stepsize sequence and some alpha > 1, such that for all L-smooth convex f, f(x_T) - f* . L ||x0 - x*||^2 / T^alpha for all T in N?
We remark that we seek an anytime, monotonically decreasing upper bound on the error: Indeed, with long steps, the errors themselves may not decrease monotonically.

needs_review.question_text_raw: We further note that while we focus on the convex setting, the analogous question for the strongly-convex case is also of interest, for which it is unclear whether any stepsize sequence achieves an anytime exp(-T / o(kappa)) rate, uniformly over functions with condition number kappa.
